public_rationale: Klarna made strong AI claims and later confirmed hiring two human agents. The causal explanation remains disputed: its regulatory response says the relevant remarks concerned human-service quality, not AI-quality problems. Renewed hiring is established, but the available records do not settle whether it demonstrates the claimed AI shortfall. Conflicting explanations alone do not justify a mixed factual verdict.
limitations: The hiring confirmation comes through reporting of a company statement.
The regulatory explanation is Klarna's own account.
The filing quotation retains the page number inserted by the page reader.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The Klarna effect, in which companies rehire humans after making extravagant claims about AI, is another sign that generative AI is still not as good as it was cracked up to be.

statement.excerpt: The Klarna effect, in which companies rehire humans after making extravagant claims around AI, is yet another sign that GenAI is still not as good as it was cracked up to be.

from_speaker: after making extravagant claims around AI
another sign that GenAI is still not as good as it was cracked up to be
our_interpretation: The checkable proposition is that renewed human hiring following AI replacement claims reflects shortcomings in deployed AI performance.
Rehire humans means resume hiring people into affected functions; it need not mean hiring the same former employees.
The contextual period runs from the August 2023 discussion through the post date and includes intervening company decisions.
A sign of limitations does not require proving that AI has no useful applications or that companies abandoned it.
criteria.support_condition: Documented AI replacement claims are followed by renewed human hiring, with credible records connecting that decision to AI performance falling short.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable records establish that the cited hiring reversal did not occur or that its attributed AI-performance explanation is incorrect.
